caption: Previous: a bar sweeping across, leaving a trail of last frames fading behind it
why: The most basic memory an effect has is its own last frame. Previous gives this pixel's colour from the frame before - fade it a little and draw the new frame over it, and anything that moves leaves a trail.

Trails, smears, afterglow, motion blur all start here. Its neighbours: Previous at reads another pixel's last colour (for things that move or spread); Blur reads it softened; Field remembers numbers rather than colours; Previous is this pixel, as it was.
steps: Previous has no inputs or settings: it is this pixel's colour from last frame. It goes into a **Fade** (keep 0.85), dimming it.
New: one narrow bar from **Stripes** (count 1, duty 0.06) sweeping across with a clock (**Time** times 0.5), in the **Palette**'s colour for its place.
A **Blend** in max mode keeps the brighter of the faded last frame and the new bar.
The bar leaves a fading tail behind it - each frame's picture is last frame's, dimmed, with the bar drawn on top.

try.label: Long tail
try.text: the Fade's keep at 0.97: the tail fades slowly and stretches across the matrix.

try.label: Short tail
try.text: the Fade's keep at 0.5: only a short smear behind the bar.

try.label: Add up
try.text: the Blend's mode add: old and new light add, so where the bar passes over its own tail it flares.
